title: Auto-reassign jobs when driver added to team or team deleted
tech: Node.js, TypeScript, Express, PostgreSQL, Prisma 6, Zod, Vitest
keyConstraints: TypeScript strict mode, Zod validation server-side, .nullish() not .optional().nullable(), Prisma selects must include all returned fields (jobInclude is source of truth), no UI component libraries, CSS Modules only
description: When a driver is added to a team, all jobs currently assigned to that driver (assignedDriverId = driverId) should be moved to the team (teamId = team.id, assignedDriverId = null). This applies regardless of whether the job has a scheduledStart. Removing a driver from a team does not change job assignments. When a team is deleted, all jobs assigned to that team are unassigned: teamId = null, assignedDriverId = null, status = DRAFT — they return to the unassigned pool.
acceptanceCriteria: PATCH /api/teams/:id adding a new member triggers reassignment: all jobs where assignedDriverId = addedDriverId are updated to teamId = teamId and assignedDriverId = null in the same transaction
PATCH /api/teams/:id removing a member does not change any job assignments
DELETE /api/teams/:id sets teamId = null, assignedDriverId = null, status = DRAFT on all jobs that had teamId = deletedTeamId, in the same transaction as the team deletion
All job updates use Prisma transactions — no partial state if something fails
Existing team delete logic that blocks deletion when active jobs are assigned is removed or updated to allow deletion (jobs are unassigned instead of blocking)
npx tsc --noEmit passes with no errors
implementationNotes: Use prisma.$transaction([]) to wrap both the team member update and the job reassignment updates atomically.

For add member: find the diff between current members and new members list to identify added drivers. For each added driver, run prisma.job.updateMany({ where: { assignedDriverId: driverId }, data: { assignedDriverId: null, teamId: teamId } }).
For remove member: no job changes needed — just update TeamMember records as before.
For DELETE /api/teams/:id: before deleting the team, run prisma.job.updateMany({ where: { teamId: id }, data: { teamId: null, assignedDriverId: null, status: 'DRAFT' } }) inside the same transaction.
The existing guard that blocks team deletion when jobs are assigned should be removed — deletion now unassigns jobs instead of blocking.
Do not rewrite working code — only modify the member diff logic and delete handler.
jobInclude in job.service.ts does not need changes — no new fields are added.
securityConsiderations: All endpoints already require adminOrDispatcher middleware. No new attack surface. Ensure job reassignment only affects jobs belonging to the correct team/driver — use exact Prisma where clauses.
